newsitem.title: USA: Wendy's CEO sees no impact from "burger war".
newsitem.headline: Wendy's CEO sees no impact from "burger war".

text.p: Wendy's International Inc does not expect a soon-to-be-offered $0.55 burger promotion by competitor McDonald's Corp to have an impact on Wendy's sales and earnings, chairman and chief executive officer Gordon Teter said Thursday.
Asked if he was concerned about such an impact on results in the short term, Teter said, "No, we're not worried."
Speaking to Reuters after a restaurant opening, he reiterated that Wendy's plans to maintain its prices.
Wendy's burger prices range from about $0.99 to about $3.74, a Cleveland-area Wendy's restaurant said.

McDonald's plans a $0.55 sandwich promotion, expected to begin in April. Teter said the deal is expected to be similar to previous McDonald's meal prices in that it would require a drink purchase. "I think consumers catch on pretty fast, and that they would just as soon go to Wendy's and get good food."
He declined comment on First Call's earnings mean estimates of $0.21 a share for the first quarter versus $0.16 a year ago and $1.40 for the 1997 year versus $1.19.
Wendy's, based in Dublin, Ohio, near Columbus, has 6,500 Wendy's hamburger and Tim Hortons coffee/pastry restaurants.
